Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 108, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

It is Meccan, and it has forty-two letters, ten words, and three verses.

Al-Ustadh Abu al-Husayn al-Farisi al-Mawardi informed me, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Shaybani related to us, saying: Abu 'Amr al-Habbari and Abu 'Uthman al-Basri related to us, the two saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-'Abdi related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾, Allah will give him to drink from the rivers of Paradise, and he will be given ten good deeds for each offering that the servants of God offer on the day of 'Id, and they will be brought near to the People of the Book and the polytheists." [271] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/458.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah related to us, saying: Abu 'Ali Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Katib related to us, saying: Nu'aym ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Nuh ibn Abi Maryam related to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, from Makhul, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾, he will have what lies between East and West: camels, on each camel scrolls, each scroll like the world and what is in it, and it will be recorded for him in fine hair, and there will be nothing in it except the description of his palaces and dwellings in Paradise." [272]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: This surah was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il ibn Hisham ibn Sa'id ibn Sahm. He saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) coming out of the mosque while he (al-'As) was entering, and they met at the gate of the Banu Sahm and talked, while some of the chiefs of Quraysh were sitting in the mosque. When al-'As entered, they said to him: "With whom were you talking?" He said: "With that one who is cut off (al-Abtar)," meaning the Prophet (ﷺ). 'Abd Allah, the son of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by Khadijah, had died before that, and they used to call anyone who had no son "abtar" (cut off). So Quraysh called him "abtar" and "sanbur" at the death of his son. Then Allah, glory be to Him, revealed ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾.

The common reading is with the letter 'ayn (ﷺ) in "a'taynaka," but al-Hasan and Talhah ibn Musarrif read "anţaynāka" with the letter nun, and this is related from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Mutawi'i informed us, with my reading to him, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Saffar al-Isfahani related to us, saying: Abu al-Muthanna Mu'adin ibn al-Muthanna ibn Mu'ad ibn Nasr al-'Ubaydi informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Muharram Abu Qatadah al-Basri related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith ibn 'Amr related to us, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salamah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: "Inna anţaynāka al-Kawthar."

Al-Kawthar is on the pattern fawʿal, derived from al-kathrah (abundance), like nawfal from al-nafl and hawqar from al-haqr. The Arabs call anything abundant in number or in quantity or in importance "kawthar." Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: It was said to an old woman whose son returned from a journey: "With what has your son returned?" She said: "He returned with kawthar," meaning with much wealth. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/216.]]

They differed concerning what is meant by it here.

Abu Muhammad al-Mukhalidi related to us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Thaqafi informed us, saying: Abu Hammam al-Walid ibn Shuja' al-Sakuni and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn Aban related to us, the two saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman related to us, from al-Mukhtar ibn Falfal, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with us, he dozed off, or he fainted, then he raised his head smiling and said: "Do you know what I laughed at?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "A surah has been revealed to me," and he recited "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar," and he recited until he finished the surah. When he had recited it, he said: "Do you know what al-Kawthar is? It is a river in Paradise which my Lord, mighty and majestic, promised me, and in it is much good. Beside that river is a basin to which my community will come on the Day of Resurrection, whose vessels are as many as the stars. A man will be pulled away from it, and I will say: 'My Lord, he is of my community.' It will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.'" [273] [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 2/43; Sahih Muslim: 1/12, with variation.]]

Abu Sa'id ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Abu 'Utbah Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Himsi related to us, saying: Ayyub ibn Suwayd related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim related to us, from his paternal uncle al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mu'ayd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ascended and recited it to the people. When he came down, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is this that Allah, glory be to Him, has given you?" He said: "A river in Paradise, whiter than milk, straighter than an arrow. Its two banks are domes of pearls, and the pearls and rubies. A green bird with necks like the necks of Bukht camels comes to it." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how pleasant this bird must be!" He said: "Shall I not tell you of something more pleasant than it?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Whoever eats of the bird and drinks of the water will attain the pleasure of Allah, glory be to Him." [274] [[Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn: 5/680.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mutayri informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, saying: 'Ata' related to us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its two banks of gold, its course over pearls and rubies, its soil more fragrant than musk, its water sweeter than honey, and whiter than snow." [275] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/423, no. 39146.]]

'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, which gurgles in the basin. Whoever wishes to hear its gurgling, let him put his two fingers in his ears."

Some of them said: It is the Basin itself. Its description, as came in the reports, is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) described the Basin of al-Kawthar, saying: "Its pebbles are red rubies, green chrysolite, pearls and coral; its mud is pure musk, and its dust is camphor. Its water is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, and colder than snow. It flows from the root of the Lote Tree (sidrah). Its width and length are between East and West. Its two banks are saffron and domes of pearls and coral. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty, and whoever performs ablution with it will never be dishevelled. In it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." Abu Bakr and 'Umar said: "Indeed, they are delicious." He said: "Eating them is more delicious than them." [276]

In another report: "This community will crowd around the Basin like the crowding of thirsty she-donkeys." [277] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/425, no. 39155.]]

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib informed us in the year three hundred and six, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Saffar al-Isfahani related to us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah al-'Umari al-Kufi informed us in Kufa, saying: Bishr ibn Dawud al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Mas'ud ibn Sabur related to us, from 'Ali ibn 'Asim, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, my Basin has four corners. The first corner is in the hand of Abu Bakr, the second in the hand of 'Umar, the third in the hand of 'Uthman, and the fourth in the hand of 'Ali. Whoever loves Abu Bakr and hates 'Umar, Abu Bakr will not give him to drink; whoever loves 'Umar and hates Abu Bakr, 'Umar will not give him to drink; whoever loves 'Uthman and hates 'Ali, 'Uthman will not give him to drink; whoever loves 'Ali and hates 'Uthman, 'Ali will not give him to drink. Whoever speaks well of Abu Bakr has established the religion; whoever speaks well of 'Umar has made the path clear; whoever speaks well of 'Uthman has been illuminated by the light of Allah; whoever speaks well of 'Ali has grasped the firmest handhold (al-'urwah al-wuthqa). Whoever speaks well of my companions is a believer, and whoever speaks ill of my companions is a hypocrite." [278]

Qatar ibn Khalifah said: I asked 'Ata' about al-Kawthar while we were circling the House, and he said: "It is a basin given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), peace and blessings be upon him, in Paradise." Humayd related from Anas, who said: We entered upon 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad while they were discussing the Basin, and I said: "I never thought I would live to see people like you disputing about the Basin. I have left behind old women, none of whom prays but asks Allah to give her to drink from the Basin of Muhammad." And in it the poet says:

O owner of the Basin, who can approach you?
And you are truly the beloved of your Lord.
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/217.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: It is abundant good. al-Hasan said: It is the great Qur'an. 'Ikrimah said: Prophethood and the Book. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It is the great matter, and he mentioned the verse of Labid:

The lord of Malhub: we were stricken by his loss,
And at al-Radda there is another kawthar.

He means: great. [[Lisan al-'Arab: 2/15; in it: "fajja'na bi-yawmihi" (stricken by his day).]]

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abbas and Yaman ibn Dhiyab said: It is the abundance of companions and followers. Ibn Kaysan said: It is a word from the earlier books, and its meaning is preference (al-iythar). al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: al-Kawthar is two things: the facilitation of the Qur'an and the lightening of the sharia.

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: al-Kawthar is a light in your heart that guided you to Me and cut you off from other than Me. And from him also: intercession (al-shafa'ah). It was said: miracles through which you increased those who answered your call. Hilal ibn Yasaq said: It is the statement "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." It was also said: understanding of the religion. And it was said: the five prayers.

﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.﴾ Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It means: indeed, some people pray to other than God and sacrifice to other than God, so ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾; let your prayer and your sacrifice be for Me alone. 'Ikrimah, 'Ata' and Qatadah said: ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ means the 'Id prayer on the day of sacrifice. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ means the obligatory dawn prayer at Muzdalifah, and ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means the camels at Mina.

Some of them said: This verse was revealed on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, when the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions were prevented from the House and were turned back. Allah, glory be to Him, commanded him to pray, sacrifice the camels, and withdraw, and he did so. This is the narration of Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, from 'Asim al-Jahdari, from his father, from 'Uqbah ibn Zabyan, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said concerning this verse ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: He placed the right hand upon the left forearm, then placed it upon his chest.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-'Attar related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Harith al-Marwazi related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Dhiyab ibn Abi al-Sa'd related to us, from 'Asim al-Jahdari, from 'Uqbah ibn Zuhayr, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: Placing the right on the left in prayer.

'Abd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Ibn Janb related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun informed us, saying: Rawh ibn al-Musayyab related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Malik al-Bakri informed me, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the saying of Allah, glory be to Him, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: Placing the right on the left in prayer at the sacrifice.

What supports this is what:

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb related to us, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Dawud related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Qabisah ibn Hulb, from his father, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to strike one of his hands upon the other during prayer.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Simak, from Qabisah ibn Hulb, from his father, who said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) placing his right hand upon his left in prayer. Hulb is a nickname, and his name is Yazid ibn Qatadah.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Harith related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr related to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, saying: Abu Ishaq related to us, from 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Wa'il, from Wa'il ibn Hujr, who said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) placing his right hand upon his left in prayer, close to the raising, and raising his hands until they reached his ears.

'Abd Allah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Abi Zaynab al-Sulami, saying: Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi related to us, from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw a man praying with his left hand placed upon his right, so he removed the left from the right and placed the right upon the left.

Abu Muhammad al-Mukhalidi informed us, saying: Abu al-Fadl Ya'qub ibn Yusuf ibn 'Asim al-Bukhari, the jurist, informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Nasrani related to us, saying: Wahb ibn Ibrahim al-Razi related to us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Isra'il ibn Hatim al-Marwazi, who was trustworthy and reliable, related to us, saying: Muqatil ibn Hayyan informed us, from Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this surah ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Jibril: "What is this sacrifice (nahirah) which my Lord has commanded me?" [279] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/557, no. 4721.]] He said: "It is not a sacrifice, but He commands you that when you enter the state of ihram for prayer, you raise your hands when you say the takbir, when you bow, when you raise your head from bowing, and when you prostrate. For it is our prayer and the prayer of the angels in the seven heavens. Indeed, every thing has an adornment, and the adornment of prayer is raising the hands at the takbir."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "Raising the hands in prayer is from humility (al-istikanah)." I said: "What is al-istikanah?" He said: "Do you not recite this verse: ﴿So they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they supplicate﴾?" [[Surat al-Mu'minun: 76.]] He said: "It means submission (al-khudu')." [280] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/557, no. 4721; Tarikh Baghdad: 14/422.]]

What supports this is what:

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Bilal informed us, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Sa'id ibn Sulayman ibn Nawfal ibn Musahiq al-'Amiri related to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Ziyad related to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that when he stood to the obligatory prayer he would say the takbir and raise his hands level with his shoulders, and would do the same when he finished his recitation and intended to bow, and when he raised his head from bowing. He would not raise his hands in any part of his prayer while seated.

Al-Shaykh al-Salih Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Alawiyah ibn Salus al-'Abdawi informed us, in Rajab of the year three hundred and eighty-four, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Azhar al-Azhari and 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Ahmad ibn Mihran al-Mudhakkir informed us, the two saying: We heard Abu Isma'il al-Tirmidhi, and Abu Muhammad al-Mukhalidi related to us by dictation, saying: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Ahmad al-Mudhakkir informed us, saying: Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sulami related to us, saying: I prayed behind Abu 'Arim, i.e., al-Nu'man, and I saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said: "What is this?" He said: "I prayed behind Hammad ibn Zayd and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed behind Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed beside 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed behind Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed behind the Prophet (ﷺ) and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing.'"

'Aqil informed me, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, concerning ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: He raises his hands from the first takbir at the opening until the sacrifice.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm informed us, saying: al-Farra' related to us, saying: It is said: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, meaning: face the qiblah with your throat (nahr). I heard some of the Arabs say: "Our dwellings face one another (tatanahar)," i.e., this one faces that one, meaning in front of it. And one of the Bani Asad recited to me:

O Abu Hakam, are you not the paternal uncle of Mujalid,
And the chief of the people of al-Abtah, the one who faces (al-mutanahir)?

Meaning: one faces the other. And to this went al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi,

[The text ends here.]

Wa-qala Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib: sa'altu 'Ata' 'an qawlihi subhanahu: ﴿wa-ankhar﴾, qala: amara Rasul Allah ﷺ an yastawiya bayna al-sajdatayn jalisan hatta yabduwa nahruhu.

Sulayman al-Taymi: ya'ni wa-arfa' yadayka bil-du'a' ila nahrika.

Dhu al-Nun: ay adhbah hawaka fi qalbika.

﴿Inna shani'aka huwa al-abtar﴾: ya'ni anna 'aduwwaka wa-mubghidaka huwa al-aqall al-adhall al-munqati' dabiruhu. Nazalat fi al-'As ibn Wa'il. Wa-qala Shamir ibn 'Atiyya: huwa 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt. Wa-qala 'Ikrima 'an Ibn 'Abbas: nazalat fi Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf wa-jama'a min Quraysh, wa-dhalika annahu lamma qadima Ka'b Makkata qalat lahu Quraysh: nahnu ahl al-saqaya wa-al-sidana wa-anta sayyid ahl al-Madina, fa-nahnu khayrun am hadha al-sunbur al-mumbatir min qawmihi?

Faqala: bal antum khayrun minhu. Fa-nazalat fi Ka'b: ﴿Alam tara ila alladhina utu nasiban mina al-kitab﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 23], al-ayah. Wa-nazalat fi alladhina qalu lil-Nabi ﷺ: abtar.

﴿Inna shani'aka huwa al-abtar﴾: ya'ni al-munqati' min kulli khayr. Qala al-Junayd: al-munqati' 'an bulugh amalihi fika.

They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "A surah has been revealed to me," and he recited "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar," and he recited until he finished the surah. When he had recited it, he said: "Do you know what al-Kawthar is? It is a river in Paradise which my Lord, mighty and majestic, promised me, and in it is much good. Beside that river is a basin to which my community will come on the Day of Resurrection, whose vessels are as many as the stars. A man will be pulled away from it, and I will say: 'My Lord, he is of my community.' It will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.'" [273] [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 2/43; Sahih Muslim: 1/12, with variation.]]

Abu Sa'id ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Abu 'Utbah Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Himsi related to us, saying: Ayyub ibn Suwayd related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim related to us, from his paternal uncle al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mu'ayd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ascended and recited it to the people. When he came down, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is this that Allah, glory be to Him, has given you?" He said: "A river in Paradise, whiter than milk, straighter than an arrow. Its two banks are domes of pearls, and the pearls and rubies. A green bird with necks like the necks of Bukht camels comes to it." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how pleasant this bird must be!" He said: "Shall I not tell you of something more pleasant than it?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Whoever eats of the bird and drinks of the water will attain the pleasure of Allah, glory be to Him." [274] [[Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn: 5/680.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mutayri informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, saying: 'Ata' related to us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its two banks of gold, its course over pearls and rubies, its soil more fragrant than musk, its water sweeter than honey, and whiter than snow." [275] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/423, no. 39146.]]

'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, which gurgles in the basin. Whoever wishes to hear its gurgling, let him put his two fingers in his ears."

Some of them said: It is the Basin itself. Its description, as came in the reports, is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) described the Basin of al-Kawthar, saying: "Its pebbles are red rubies, green chrysolite, pearls and coral; its mud is pure musk, and its dust is camphor. Its water is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, and colder than snow. It flows from the root of the Lote Tree (sidrah). Its width and length are between East and West. Its two banks are saffron and domes of pearls and coral. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty, and whoever performs ablution with it will never be dishevelled. In it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." Abu Bakr and 'Umar said: "Indeed, they are delicious." He said: "Eating them is more delicious than them." [276]

In another report: "This community will crowd around the Basin like the crowding of thirsty she-donkeys." [277] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/425, no. 39155.]]

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib informed us in the year three hundred and six, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Saffar al-Isfahani related to us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah al-'Umari al-Kufi informed us in Kufa, saying: Bishr ibn Dawud al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Mas'ud ibn Sabur related to us, from 'Ali ibn 'Asim, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, my Basin has four corners. The first corner is in the hand of Abu Bakr, the second in the hand of 'Umar, the third in the hand of 'Uthman, and the fourth in the hand of 'Ali. Whoever loves Abu Bakr and hates 'Umar, Abu Bakr will not give him to drink; whoever loves 'Umar and hates Abu Bakr, 'Umar will not give him to drink; whoever loves 'Uthman and hates 'Ali, 'Uthman will not give him to drink; whoever loves 'Ali and hates 'Uthman, 'Ali will not give him to drink. Whoever speaks well of Abu Bakr has established the religion; whoever speaks well of 'Umar has made the path clear; whoever speaks well of 'Uthman has been illuminated by the light of Allah; whoever speaks well of 'Ali has grasped the firmest handhold (al-'urwah al-wuthqa). Whoever speaks well of my companions is a believer, and whoever speaks ill of my companions is a hypocrite." [278]

Qatar ibn Khalifah said: I asked 'Ata' about al-Kawthar while we were circling the House, and he said: "It is a basin given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), peace and blessings be upon him, in Paradise." Humayd related from Anas, who said: We entered upon 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad while they were discussing the Basin, and I said: "I never thought I would live to see people like you disputing about the Basin. I have left behind old women, none of whom prays but asks Allah to give her to drink from the Basin of Muhammad." And in it the poet says:

O owner of the Basin, who can approach you?
And you are truly the beloved of your Lord.
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/217.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: It is abundant good. al-Hasan said: It is the great Qur'an. 'Ikrimah said: Prophethood and the Book. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It is the great matter, and he mentioned the verse of Labid:

The lord of Malhub: we were stricken by his loss,
And at al-Radda there is another kawthar.

He means: great. [[Lisan al-'Arab: 2/15; in it: "fajja'na bi-yawmihi" (stricken by his day).]]

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abbas and Yaman ibn Dhiyab said: It is the abundance of companions and followers. Ibn Kaysan said: It is a word from the earlier books, and its meaning is preference (al-iythar). al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: al-Kawthar is two things: the facilitation of the Qur'an and the lightening of the sharia.

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: al-Kawthar is a light in your heart that guided you to Me and cut you off from other than Me. And from him also: intercession (al-shafa'ah). It was said: miracles through which you increased those who answered your call. Hilal ibn Yasaq said: It is the statement "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." It was also said: understanding of the religion. And it was said: the five prayers.

﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.﴾ Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It means: indeed, some people pray to other than God and sacrifice to other than God, so ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾; let your prayer and your sacrifice be for Me alone. 'Ikrimah, 'Ata' and Qatadah said: ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ means the 'Id prayer on the day of sacrifice. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ means the obligatory dawn prayer at Muzdalifah, and ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means the camels at Mina.

Some of them said: This verse was revealed on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, when the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions were prevented from the House and were turned back. Allah, glory be to Him, commanded him to pray, sacrifice the camels, and withdraw, and he did so. This is the narration of Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, from 'Asim al-Jahdari, from his father, from 'Uqbah ibn Zabyan, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said concerning this verse ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: He placed the right hand upon the left forearm, then placed it upon his chest.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-'Attar related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Harith al-Marwazi related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Dhiyab ibn Abi al-Sa'd related to us, from 'Asim al-Jahdari, from 'Uqbah ibn Zuhayr, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: Placing the right on the left in prayer.

'Abd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Ibn Janb related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun informed us, saying: Rawh ibn al-Musayyab related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Malik al-Bakri informed me, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the saying of Allah, glory be to Him, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: Placing the right on the left in prayer at the sacrifice.

What supports this is what:

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb related to us, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Dawud related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Qabisah ibn Hulb, from his father, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to strike one of his hands upon the other during prayer.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Simak, from Qabisah ibn Hulb, from his father, who said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) placing his right hand upon his left in prayer. Hulb is a nickname, and his name is Yazid ibn Qatadah.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Harith related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr related to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, saying: Abu Ishaq related to us, from 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Wa'il, from Wa'il ibn Hujr, who said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) placing his right hand upon his left in prayer, close to the raising, and raising his hands until they reached his ears.

'Abd Allah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Abi Zaynab al-Sulami, saying: Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi related to us, from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw a man praying with his left hand placed upon his right, so he removed the left from the right and placed the right upon the left.

Abu Muhammad al-Mukhalidi informed us, saying: Abu al-Fadl Ya'qub ibn Yusuf ibn 'Asim al-Bukhari, the jurist, informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Nasrani related to us, saying: Wahb ibn Ibrahim al-Razi related to us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Isra'il ibn Hatim al-Marwazi, who was trustworthy and reliable, related to us, saying: Muqatil ibn Hayyan informed us, from Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this surah ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Jibril: "What is this sacrifice (nahirah) which my Lord has commanded me?" [279] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/557, no. 4721.]] He said: "It is not a sacrifice, but He commands you that when you enter the state of ihram for prayer, you raise your hands when you say the takbir, when you bow, when you raise your head from bowing, and when you prostrate. For it is our prayer and the prayer of the angels in the seven heavens. Indeed, every thing has an adornment, and the adornment of prayer is raising the hands at the takbir."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "Raising the hands in prayer is from humility (al-istikanah)." I said: "What is al-istikanah?" He said: "Do you not recite this verse: ﴿So they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they supplicate﴾?" [[Surat al-Mu'minun: 76.]] He said: "It means submission (al-khudu')." [280] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/557, no. 4721; Tarikh Baghdad: 14/422.]]

What supports this is what:

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Bilal informed us, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Sa'id ibn Sulayman ibn Nawfal ibn Musahiq al-'Amiri related to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Ziyad related to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that when he stood to the obligatory prayer he would say the takbir and raise his hands level with his shoulders, and would do the same when he finished his recitation and intended to bow, and when he raised his head from bowing. He would not raise his hands in any part of his prayer while seated.

Al-Shaykh al-Salih Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Alawiyah ibn Salus al-'Abdawi informed us, in Rajab of the year three hundred and eighty-four, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Azhar al-Azhari and 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Ahmad ibn Mihran al-Mudhakkir informed us, the two saying: We heard Abu Isma'il al-Tirmidhi, and Abu Muhammad al-Mukhalidi related to us by dictation, saying: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Ahmad al-Mudhakkir informed us, saying: Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sulami related to us, saying: I prayed behind Abu 'Arim, i.e., al-Nu'man, and I saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said: "What is this?" He said: "I prayed behind Hammad ibn Zayd and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed behind Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed beside 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed behind Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed behind the Prophet (ﷺ) and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing.'"

'Aqil informed me, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, concerning ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: He raises his hands from the first takbir at the opening until the sacrifice.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm informed us, saying: al-Farra' related to us, saying: It is said: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, meaning: face the qiblah with your throat (nahr). I heard some of the Arabs say: "Our dwellings face one another (tatanahar)," i.e., this one faces that one, meaning in front of it. And one of the Bani Asad recited to me:

O Abu Hakam, are you not the paternal uncle of Mujalid,
And the chief of the people of al-Abtah, the one who faces (al-mutanahir)?

Meaning: one faces the other. And to this went al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi,

[The text ends here.]

Wa-qala Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib: sa'altu 'Ata' 'an qawlihi subhanahu: ﴿wa-ankhar﴾, qala: amara Rasul Allah ﷺ an yastawiya bayna al-sajdatayn jalisan hatta yabduwa nahruhu.

Sulayman al-Taymi: ya'ni wa-arfa' yadayka bil-du'a' ila nahrika.

Dhu al-Nun: ay adhbah hawaka fi qalbika.

﴿Inna shani'aka huwa al-abtar﴾: ya'ni anna 'aduwwaka wa-mubghidaka huwa al-aqall al-adhall al-munqati' dabiruhu. Nazalat fi al-'As ibn Wa'il. Wa-qala Shamir ibn 'Atiyya: huwa 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt. Wa-qala 'Ikrima 'an Ibn 'Abbas: nazalat fi Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf wa-jama'a min Quraysh, wa-dhalika annahu lamma qadima Ka'b Makkata qalat lahu Quraysh: nahnu ahl al-saqaya wa-al-sidana wa-anta sayyid ahl al-Madina, fa-nahnu khayrun am hadha al-sunbur al-mumbatir min qawmihi?

Faqala: bal antum khayrun minhu. Fa-nazalat fi Ka'b: ﴿Alam tara ila alladhina utu nasiban mina al-kitab﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 23], al-ayah. Wa-nazalat fi alladhina qalu lil-Nabi ﷺ: abtar.

﴿Inna shani'aka huwa al-abtar﴾: ya'ni al-munqati' min kulli khayr. Qala al-Junayd: al-munqati' 'an bulugh amalihi fika.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 108, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

It is Meccan, and it has forty-two letters, ten words, and three verses.

Al-Ustadh Abu al-Husayn al-Farisi al-Mawardi informed me, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Shaybani related to us, saying: Abu 'Amr al-Habbari and Abu 'Uthman al-Basri related to us, the two saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-'Abdi related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾, Allah will give him to drink from the rivers of Paradise, and he will be given ten good deeds for each offering that the servants of God offer on the day of 'Id, and they will be brought near to the People of the Book and the polytheists." [271] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/458.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah related to us, saying: Abu 'Ali Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Katib related to us, saying: Nu'aym ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Nuh ibn Abi Maryam related to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, from Makhul, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾, he will have what lies between East and West: camels, on each camel scrolls, each scroll like the world and what is in it, and it will be recorded for him in fine hair, and there will be nothing in it except the description of his palaces and dwellings in Paradise." [272]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: This surah was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il ibn Hisham ibn Sa'id ibn Sahm. He saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) coming out of the mosque while he (al-'As) was entering, and they met at the gate of the Banu Sahm and talked, while some of the chiefs of Quraysh were sitting in the mosque. When al-'As entered, they said to him: "With whom were you talking?" He said: "With that one who is cut off (al-Abtar)," meaning the Prophet (ﷺ). 'Abd Allah, the son of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by Khadijah, had died before that, and they used to call anyone who had no son "abtar" (cut off). So Quraysh called him "abtar" and "sanbur" at the death of his son. Then Allah, glory be to Him, revealed ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾.

The common reading is with the letter 'ayn (ﷺ) in "a'taynaka," but al-Hasan and Talhah ibn Musarrif read "anţaynāka" with the letter nun, and this is related from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Mutawi'i informed us, with my reading to him, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Saffar al-Isfahani related to us, saying: Abu al-Muthanna Mu'adin ibn al-Muthanna ibn Mu'ad ibn Nasr al-'Ubaydi informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Muharram Abu Qatadah al-Basri related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith ibn 'Amr related to us, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salamah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: "Inna anţaynāka al-Kawthar."

Al-Kawthar is on the pattern fawʿal, derived from al-kathrah (abundance), like nawfal from al-nafl and hawqar from al-haqr. The Arabs call anything abundant in number or in quantity or in importance "kawthar." Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: It was said to an old woman whose son returned from a journey: "With what has your son returned?" She said: "He returned with kawthar," meaning with much wealth. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/216.]]

They differed concerning what is meant by it here.

Abu Muhammad al-Mukhalidi related to us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Thaqafi informed us, saying: Abu Hammam al-Walid ibn Shuja' al-Sakuni and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn Aban related to us, the two saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman related to us, from al-Mukhtar ibn Falfal, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with us, he dozed off, or he fainted, then he raised his head smiling and said: "Do you know what I laughed at?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "A surah has been revealed to me," and he recited "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar," and he recited until he finished the surah. When he had recited it, he said: "Do you know what al-Kawthar is? It is a river in Paradise which my Lord, mighty and majestic, promised me, and in it is much good. Beside that river is a basin to which my community will come on the Day of Resurrection, whose vessels are as many as the stars. A man will be pulled away from it, and I will say: 'My Lord, he is of my community.' It will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.'" [273] [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 2/43; Sahih Muslim: 1/12, with variation.]]

Abu Sa'id ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Abu 'Utbah Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Himsi related to us, saying: Ayyub ibn Suwayd related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim related to us, from his paternal uncle al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mu'ayd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ascended and recited it to the people. When he came down, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is this that Allah, glory be to Him, has given you?" He said: "A river in Paradise, whiter than milk, straighter than an arrow. Its two banks are domes of pearls, and the pearls and rubies. A green bird with necks like the necks of Bukht camels comes to it." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how pleasant this bird must be!" He said: "Shall I not tell you of something more pleasant than it?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Whoever eats of the bird and drinks of the water will attain the pleasure of Allah, glory be to Him." [274] [[Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn: 5/680.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mutayri informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, saying: 'Ata' related to us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its two banks of gold, its course over pearls and rubies, its soil more fragrant than musk, its water sweeter than honey, and whiter than snow." [275] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/423, no. 39146.]]

'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, which gurgles in the basin. Whoever wishes to hear its gurgling, let him put his two fingers in his ears."

Some of them said: It is the Basin itself. Its description, as came in the reports, is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) described the Basin of al-Kawthar, saying: "Its pebbles are red rubies, green chrysolite, pearls and coral; its mud is pure musk, and its dust is camphor. Its water is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, and colder than snow. It flows from the root of the Lote Tree (sidrah). Its width and length are between East and West. Its two banks are saffron and domes of pearls and coral. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty, and whoever performs ablution with it will never be dishevelled. In it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." Abu Bakr and 'Umar said: "Indeed, they are delicious." He said: "Eating them is more delicious than them." [276]

In another report: "This community will crowd around the Basin like the crowding of thirsty she-donkeys." [277] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/425, no. 39155.]]

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib informed us in the year three hundred and six, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Saffar al-Isfahani related to us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah al-'Umari al-Kufi informed us in Kufa, saying: Bishr ibn Dawud al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Mas'ud ibn Sabur related to us, from 'Ali ibn 'Asim, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, my Basin has four corners. The first corner is in the hand of Abu Bakr, the second in the hand of 'Umar, the third in the hand of 'Uthman, and the fourth in the hand of 'Ali. Whoever loves Abu Bakr and hates 'Umar, Abu Bakr will not give him to drink; whoever loves 'Umar and hates Abu Bakr, 'Umar will not give him to drink; whoever loves 'Uthman and hates 'Ali, 'Uthman will not give him to drink; whoever loves 'Ali and hates 'Uthman, 'Ali will not give him to drink. Whoever speaks well of Abu Bakr has established the religion; whoever speaks well of 'Umar has made the path clear; whoever speaks well of 'Uthman has been illuminated by the light of Allah; whoever speaks well of 'Ali has grasped the firmest handhold (al-'urwah al-wuthqa). Whoever speaks well of my companions is a believer, and whoever speaks ill of my companions is a hypocrite." [278]

Qatar ibn Khalifah said: I asked 'Ata' about al-Kawthar while we were circling the House, and he said: "It is a basin given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), peace and blessings be upon him, in Paradise." Humayd related from Anas, who said: We entered upon 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad while they were discussing the Basin, and I said: "I never thought I would live to see people like you disputing about the Basin. I have left behind old women, none of whom prays but asks Allah to give her to drink from the Basin of Muhammad." And in it the poet says:

O owner of the Basin, who can approach you?
And you are truly the beloved of your Lord.
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/217.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: It is abundant good. al-Hasan said: It is the great Qur'an. 'Ikrimah said: Prophethood and the Book. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It is the great matter, and he mentioned the verse of Labid:

The lord of Malhub: we were stricken by his loss,
And at al-Radda there is another kawthar.

He means: great. [[Lisan al-'Arab: 2/15; in it: "fajja'na bi-yawmihi" (stricken by his day).]]

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abbas and Yaman ibn Dhiyab said: It is the abundance of companions and followers. Ibn Kaysan said: It is a word from the earlier books, and its meaning is preference (al-iythar). al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: al-Kawthar is two things: the facilitation of the Qur'an and the lightening of the sharia.

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: al-Kawthar is a light in your heart that guided you to Me and cut you off from other than Me. And from him also: intercession (al-shafa'ah). It was said: miracles through which you increased those who answered your call. Hilal ibn Yasaq said: It is the statement "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." It was also said: understanding of the religion. And it was said: the five prayers.

﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.﴾ Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It means: indeed, some people pray to other than God and sacrifice to other than God, so ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾; let your prayer and your sacrifice be for Me alone. 'Ikrimah, 'Ata' and Qatadah said: ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ means the 'Id prayer on the day of sacrifice. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ means the obligatory dawn prayer at Muzdalifah, and ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means the camels at Mina.

Some of them said: This verse was revealed on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, when the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions were prevented from the House and were turned back. Allah, glory be to Him, commanded him to pray, sacrifice the camels, and withdraw, and he did so. This is the narration of Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, from 'Asim al-Jahdari, from his father, from 'Uqbah ibn Zabyan, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said concerning this verse ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: He placed the right hand upon the left forearm, then placed it upon his chest.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-'Attar related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Harith al-Marwazi related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Dhiyab ibn Abi al-Sa'd related to us, from 'Asim al-Jahdari, from 'Uqbah ibn Zuhayr, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: Placing the right on the left in prayer.

'Abd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Ibn Janb related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun informed us, saying: Rawh ibn al-Musayyab related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Malik al-Bakri informed me, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the saying of Allah, glory be to Him, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: Placing the right on the left in prayer at the sacrifice.

What supports this is what:

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb related to us, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Dawud related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Qabisah ibn Hulb, from his father, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to strike one of his hands upon the other during prayer.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Simak, from Qabisah ibn Hulb, from his father, who said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) placing his right hand upon his left in prayer. Hulb is a nickname, and his name is Yazid ibn Qatadah.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Harith related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr related to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, saying: Abu Ishaq related to us, from 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Wa'il, from Wa'il ibn Hujr, who said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) placing his right hand upon his left in prayer, close to the raising, and raising his hands until they reached his ears.

'Abd Allah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Abi Zaynab al-Sulami, saying: Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi related to us, from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw a man praying with his left hand placed upon his right, so he removed the left from the right and placed the right upon the left.

Abu Muhammad al-Mukhalidi informed us, saying: Abu al-Fadl Ya'qub ibn Yusuf ibn 'Asim al-Bukhari, the jurist, informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Nasrani related to us, saying: Wahb ibn Ibrahim al-Razi related to us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Isra'il ibn Hatim al-Marwazi, who was trustworthy and reliable, related to us, saying: Muqatil ibn Hayyan informed us, from Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this surah ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Jibril: "What is this sacrifice (nahirah) which my Lord has commanded me?" [279] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/557, no. 4721.]] He said: "It is not a sacrifice, but He commands you that when you enter the state of ihram for prayer, you raise your hands when you say the takbir, when you bow, when you raise your head from bowing, and when you prostrate. For it is our prayer and the prayer of the angels in the seven heavens. Indeed, every thing has an adornment, and the adornment of prayer is raising the hands at the takbir."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "Raising the hands in prayer is from humility (al-istikanah)." I said: "What is al-istikanah?" He said: "Do you not recite this verse: ﴿So they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they supplicate﴾?" [[Surat al-Mu'minun: 76.]] He said: "It means submission (al-khudu')." [280] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/557, no. 4721; Tarikh Baghdad: 14/422.]]

What supports this is what:

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Bilal informed us, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Sa'id ibn Sulayman ibn Nawfal ibn Musahiq al-'Amiri related to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Ziyad related to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that when he stood to the obligatory prayer he would say the takbir and raise his hands level with his shoulders, and would do the same when he finished his recitation and intended to bow, and when he raised his head from bowing. He would not raise his hands in any part of his prayer while seated.

Al-Shaykh al-Salih Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Alawiyah ibn Salus al-'Abdawi informed us, in Rajab of the year three hundred and eighty-four, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Azhar al-Azhari and 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Ahmad ibn Mihran al-Mudhakkir informed us, the two saying: We heard Abu Isma'il al-Tirmidhi, and Abu Muhammad al-Mukhalidi related to us by dictation, saying: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Ahmad al-Mudhakkir informed us, saying: Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sulami related to us, saying: I prayed behind Abu 'Arim, i.e., al-Nu'man, and I saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said: "What is this?" He said: "I prayed behind Hammad ibn Zayd and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed behind Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed beside 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed behind Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing. I said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'I prayed behind the Prophet (ﷺ) and saw him raising his hands when he began the prayer, when he bowed, and when he raised his head from bowing.'"

'Aqil informed me, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, concerning ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: He raises his hands from the first takbir at the opening until the sacrifice.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm informed us, saying: al-Farra' related to us, saying: It is said: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, meaning: face the qiblah with your throat (nahr). I heard some of the Arabs say: "Our dwellings face one another (tatanahar)," i.e., this one faces that one, meaning in front of it. And one of the Bani Asad recited to me:

O Abu Hakam, are you not the paternal uncle of Mujalid,
And the chief of the people of al-Abtah, the one who faces (al-mutanahir)?

Meaning: one faces the other. And to this went al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi,

[The text ends here.]

Wa-qala Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib: sa'altu 'Ata' 'an qawlihi subhanahu: ﴿wa-ankhar﴾, qala: amara Rasul Allah ﷺ an yastawiya bayna al-sajdatayn jalisan hatta yabduwa nahruhu.

Sulayman al-Taymi: ya'ni wa-arfa' yadayka bil-du'a' ila nahrika.

Dhu al-Nun: ay adhbah hawaka fi qalbika.

﴿Inna shani'aka huwa al-abtar﴾: ya'ni anna 'aduwwaka wa-mubghidaka huwa al-aqall al-adhall al-munqati' dabiruhu. Nazalat fi al-'As ibn Wa'il. Wa-qala Shamir ibn 'Atiyya: huwa 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt. Wa-qala 'Ikrima 'an Ibn 'Abbas: nazalat fi Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf wa-jama'a min Quraysh, wa-dhalika annahu lamma qadima Ka'b Makkata qalat lahu Quraysh: nahnu ahl al-saqaya wa-al-sidana wa-anta sayyid ahl al-Madina, fa-nahnu khayrun am hadha al-sunbur al-mumbatir min qawmihi?

Faqala: bal antum khayrun minhu. Fa-nazalat fi Ka'b: ﴿Alam tara ila alladhina utu nasiban mina al-kitab﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 23], al-ayah. Wa-nazalat fi alladhina qalu lil-Nabi ﷺ: abtar.

﴿Inna shani'aka huwa al-abtar﴾: ya'ni al-munqati' min kulli khayr. Qala al-Junayd: al-munqati' 'an bulugh amalihi fika.
